tasks.short: Design a patient education programme with decision information: needs, content, review, approval, publishing and nurse training.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist finds what patients need to know for their treatment decisions from questions and feedback
Clinical nurse specialist collects existing patient information and decision aids
Clinical nurse specialist writes the education programs: sessions, leaflets and option comparisons

loop.input: The education goals, the hospital's approved leaflets and vetted public patient texts, and the target reading level.
loop.output: Session outlines, plain-language leaflet text and an option comparison table (benefits, risks, what happens next) per treatment choice.
loop.check: Every statement must cite a paragraph of an approved source; risks and numbers in the option table must equal the source wording; reading-level score must fall in the set band; no advice favours one option unless the source does.
loop.stop: One draft per module and one redraft; then the clinical nurse specialist writes the module.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning several clinical sources into balanced plain language for a decision is writing; a template cannot do it.

steps.what: Patient panel reviews the materials for clarity
Physicians check the medical content
Patient education committee approves the final programme
Clinical nurse specialist lays out and publishes the materials on the portal and in print
Clinical nurse specialist trains nurses to deliver the programme

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts session outlines, leaflet text and option tables from the hospital's approved leaflets and vetted public patient information, citing a source paragraph for every statement, for the clinical nurse specialist to edit. After the patient panel, physicians and committee have reviewed, the approved version is laid out from the house template and published to the patient portal in the {CMS} and the print file.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each programme was written from scratch, and layout and publishing were done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted, guideline-based patient information exists, and language models can rewrite it into plain language when each sentence must cite its source.
tasks.still_hard: Balanced decision information is hard to write; drafts can tilt towards one option, and the inspectorate expects careful use of generative tools.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which choices patients struggle with and what they need to hear to decide for themselves.

ambition.what: Patients with low health literacy who get decision information at their reading level for every common treatment choice.

tasks.altitude: The clinical nurse specialist edits drafts and leads review; approval stays with the committee.

reach.learn: Whether source-cited drafts shorten their review cycle.

evidence.claim: A Dutch public patient information site offers guideline-based texts written with GP, specialist and patient organisations.
Patient education drafted only from vetted texts, each citing its paragraph, is a workable pattern.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, train, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from education goals to nurses trained to deliver; delivering the programme to patients is outside.
Input contract: approved leaflets kept by the patient education committee; vetted public texts the hospital may reuse; house template kept by communications; fallback is writing by hand.
Patient panel, physician and committee time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.
Needs finding, source collection and nurse training do not change.
unknowns: Whether the hospital may reuse public patient texts.
Number of programmes developed per year.
research_questions: Do option tables at the right reading level change how prepared patients feel for the decision?

already_counted.description: Clinical nurse specialist checks every drafted statement against its cited source.

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist keeps the source library and reading-level settings current.
Patient education committee keeps the approved source list current.

approvals.approved_version: The programme materials as approved by the committee in s6; any edit needs a new approval before publishing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Topics with no vetted public source, such as local procedures, are still written by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work on a clinical study: review the protocol, pre-screen records, fill case report forms, track compliance and meet monitors and inspectors.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist reviews the study protocol for feasibility on the ward
Clinical nurse specialist screens patient records one by one against inclusion criteria
Clinical nurse specialist copies study data from records into the case report form
Clinical nurse specialist tracks visit windows, samples and deviations for compliance in a spreadsheet
Clinical nurse specialist meets the sponsor's monitor and answers data queries
Clinical nurse specialist prepares for and meets regulatory authorities during inspections
Principal investigator reviews deviations and signs off the study files

tasks.design: A pre-screening query on the {DATA_PLATFORM} lists patients who meet the structured inclusion criteria (age, diagnosis codes, lab values); free-text criteria are still checked in the record. Mapped record fields pre-fill the case report form for the clinical nurse specialist to verify against source before saving, and a study calendar per participant built from the protocol schedule flags due visits, missed samples and deviations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Screening and data entry meant reading records and retyping values, with compliance tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Governed data platforms query record fields, and record-to-study-form transfer and study calendars exist as standard tooling.
tasks.still_hard: Each study needs its own field mapping and approval; free-text criteria and source verification stay manual.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining the study to patients and staff, and answering monitors and inspectors with confidence.

ambition.what: Every eligible patient on the ward checked for open studies, not only those the team remembers.

tasks.altitude: The clinical nurse specialist verifies pre-filled data and acts on flags instead of retyping and counting.

reach.learn: Whether one study calendar format works for all sponsors.

evidence.claim: Record-to-study-form transfer and study calendars are available tools in hospital research settings.
Medicine trials follow the EU clinical trials rules and good clinical practice, including source data verification and inspections.
Health data is special category data; research use needs a lawful basis and safeguards.

assumptions: Boundary: from protocol review to inspection; patient consent conversations and study treatment are outside.

Input contract: inclusion criteria translated into record fields by the research data manager; field mapping per study agreed with the sponsor; pre-screening allowed under the hospital's research rules and the study's ethics approval; fallback is reading records.
Principal investigator time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.
Monitor visits and inspections do not change.
unknowns: Whether the sponsor's study form accepts transferred data.
Number of studies the clinical nurse specialist supports.
research_questions: How many eligible patients does the query find that manual screening missed?

already_counted.description: Clinical nurse specialist checks the pre-screen list against the free-text criteria.
Clinical nurse specialist verifies pre-filled form values against the source.
Clinical nurse specialist reviews deviation flags.

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist helps map study fields to record fields for each new study.
Research data manager builds and maintains queries and mappings.

approvals.approved_version: Form values as verified against source by the clinical nurse specialist before saving; later changes go through the form's audit-trailed query.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Small studies that do not justify a field mapping, or criteria that are mostly free text, keep manual screening and entry.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Help ward nurses build a care plan for a complex patient, agree it with patient, family and team, and evaluate it.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist reviews the patient's problems with the ward nurse
Clinical nurse specialist writes care and treatment plans from scratch in the record
Clinical nurse specialist agrees the plan with the patient and family
Clinical nurse specialist coordinates the plan with physician, physiotherapist and others
Physician agrees the treatment parts of the plan
Clinical nurse specialist explains the plan to ward nurses at handover
Clinical nurse specialist evaluates goals after a week by reading notes

tasks.design: The clinical nurse specialists keep a library of standard care plans for complex conditions (chronic wounds, palliative care, delirium, complex pain) in the electronic health record ({OTHER}); a plan is selected and personalised rather than written from scratch. Each goal carries a measurable target, so a goal view shows progress at evaluation; conversations and coordination stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every complex plan was written from scratch, and progress had to be read from notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Records support care plan libraries and goal tracking as configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Complex patients rarely fit a standard plan; personalising is the expert work.
tasks.human_edge: Fitting the plan to this patient's wishes and to what the ward can actually deliver.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less writing per plan.

reach.task: Use standard plans for common complex problems
reach.learn: Whether ward nurses can start a plan before the specialist arrives.

evidence.claim: Records support standard care plan libraries and measurable goal tracking.
The record is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from reviewing problems to evaluating the plan; delivering care is outside.
Input contract: standard plans written and kept by the clinical nurse specialists from guidelines; goal targets entered when the plan is personalised; fallback is free text.
Physician time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.
Conversations, coordination and handover do not change.
unknowns: How many complex plans per month the clinical nurse specialist helps with.
Whether the record has a care plan library.
research_questions: Do standard plans with measurable goals change how often plans are evaluated on time?

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist keeps the standard plan library current with guidelines.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Patients with rare combinations of problems still need plans written from scratch.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign specialised therapy tasks to qualified nurses, supervise and coach at the bedside, and follow up on issues.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist decides which nurse delivers which therapy
Clinical nurse specialist checks a paper list of who is qualified for the therapy
Clinical nurse specialist supervises nursing staff delivering patient therapy at the bedside
Clinical nurse specialist gives feedback and corrects technique
Clinical nurse specialist writes supervision notes and follow-up points
Nursing manager handles performance issues raised

tasks.design: Signed-off competences from the {LMS} show next to each therapy on the unit's assignment screen, so qualification is checked at a glance instead of on paper lists. Supervision notes use a short template in the learning record that only the nurse, the clinical nurse specialist and the manager can see; supervision itself stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Qualification lists were paper and out of date.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems hold sign-offs and can show them in other screens through standard integration.
tasks.still_hard: Supervision is watching and coaching; per-nurse records raise works council questions.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a nurse's technique slip and correcting it without undermining their confidence.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; qualification checks take seconds.

reach.task: Plan refresher training for expiring therapy skills
reach.learn: Whether assignment-screen gaps show where refreshers are needed.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can expose signed-off competences to other hospital screens.
A system fit to monitor staff performance needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from assigning therapy to follow-up of issues; therapy orders are outside.
Input contract: competence sign-offs recorded in the learning system by assessors; therapy-to-skill mapping set by the clinical nurse specialists; fallback is the paper list.
Nursing manager time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.
Supervision and feedback do not change.
unknowns: Whether competence records in the learning system are complete.
How often therapy assignments change per week.
research_questions: Does showing qualification at assignment reduce therapy given by unqualified staff?

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist keeps the therapy-to-skill mapping current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Units whose sign-offs are not kept in the learning system keep paper lists.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The clinical nurse specialist keeps teaching, supervising and judgement; writing programmes, study forms and plans shifts to editing and checking.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted patient materials against sources
role.ambitious_version: A clinical nurse specialist who offers decision information every patient can read and finds every eligible patient for research.
